name: C — X3D-First Value (cheapest build that still feels fast in modded Minecraft)
target: Modded Minecraft + shaders at 1080p/1440p, 16-24 chunks, lighter 64-128x packs

cpu.name: AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D
cpu.why: Yes, the $484 CPU is in the cheap build. In Minecraft the CPU decides your chunk-render distance, tick rate and 1% lows; a 6-core non-X3D chip with a bigger GPU feels worse. If you must cut it, a Ryzen 5 9600X ($219) saves $265 but costs ~20-30% of chunk-load speed and stutters.

cooler.name: Thermalright Peerless Assassin 120 SE V2
cooler.why: Cheapest cooler that is genuinely sufficient for a 120 W X3D part.

motherboard.name: Gigabyte B850 Eagle WiFi 6E
motherboard.why: Cheapest board I would put an X3D chip in: real VRM heatsinks, PCIe 5.0 x16, BIOS flashback.

memory.name: 32 GB (2x16 GB) DDR5-6000 CL30 EXPO
memory.why: Note the absurdity of Nov 2026: the RAM costs more than the CPU. 32 GB / 2 sticks is the correct call for AM5; do not buy 4 sticks.

gpu.name: AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT 16 GB
gpu.why: 16 GB VRAM is the point — it runs Iris shaders + Distant Horizons + a 128x pack without texture thrash. It is the cheapest card worth buying for this use case, and it is excellent on Bazzite.

storage.name: WD_BLACK SN850X 2 TB NVMe
storage.why: Keep the big drive — modpack instances are 20-60 GB each and NAND prices are climbing, so buy capacity once.

psu.name: MSI MPG A1000GS 1000 W (ATX 3.1, 80+ Gold)
psu.why: Overkill for 280 W of load, but it is cheaper on sale than the 650-750 W units it beats, and it makes the next GPU upgrade free.

monitor.name: Acer Nitro VG277U 27" 1440p 180 Hz IPS (budget option)
monitor.why: If the OLED is too much, this keeps 1440p + high refresh; shaders still look great, you lose HDR contrast.
